summary: Request: Read-only, scoped inspection of prod KV-cache entries for privacy triage
description: Issue summary: Security & CS ask for a timeboxed, read-only inspection of a narrowly-scoped set of KV-cache keys in production to triage a customer privacy concern. Impact: Customer has reported that an application user may have submitted a sensitive identifier which might be present in the runtime KV cache. Team asked for a minimal, auditable snapshot to confirm presence/absence and then delete/redact if needed. This is an internal-only access request with strict redaction & audit requirements.
impact: Potential exposure of sensitive identifier for a single customer session. Customer impacted indirectly; no confirmed breach. Business impact: heightened privacy/regulatory risk if handled incorrectly. Urgency: requires same-week turn around to respond to customer compliance timeline.
requested_scope:
- Scope to keys matching prefix 'session:kv:customer-ACME-2026-03' and time window 2026-03-08T00:00Z..2026-03-10T12:00Z
- Read-only access; no export of raw payloads outside the secured audit container
- Mandatory automated redaction of high-entropy token-like strings and email-like patterns in any displayed outputs
- Access to be granted to two named engineers for max 6 hours, with session recording and token-level audit
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer reports suspicious payload referencing an internal identifier in support ticket #CUS-10921.
2) CS asks SRE to confirm whether the identifier appears in runtime KV cache for the customer's tenant.
3) Developer reproduction not possible without scoped prod access due to ephemeral nature of KV entries.
logs: Search attempted in staging using sampled keys, no match found (staging uses different tenant hash).
Partial trace from routing logs (trace id: 7f4a9dcb) shows degraded hit-rate for prefix 'session:kv:customer-ACME-2026-03'.
Console alert: 'kv-cache:eviction-threshold-nearing' at 2026-03-09T22:14:03Z — likely explains short TTLs.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Sensitive value present in KV cache but evicted before usual retention window due to bursty traffic and TTL policy.
Hypothesis B: Value persisted only in transient in-memory shard for that region and not replicated; read must be executed in-prod region to confirm.
SRE note (2026-03-11): We can mount a read-only inspector that queries specific keys via internal admin API with a safelist and masking plugin; requires IAM approval and audit recording.
Security note: Any extracted snippets must be tokenized by our redaction lambda before being written to Confluence or shared with CS.
proposed_action: 1) Approve timeboxed read-only inspector run limited to the explicit key prefix and time window. 2) Provision temporary IAM role 'int/kv-inspector/INT-402158' scoped to admin-api:ReadKeys for those keys only. 3) Run inspector in audit container; output goes through redaction pipeline (lambda v2) before any human review. 4) Record session, retain full audit logs for 12 months. 5) Deliver an artifact to CS: redaction-verified statement and evidence of presence/absence (no raw payloads).
comments: Aisha Kumar (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Customer ACME sent legal request asking to confirm whether the submitted customer identifier persisted anywhere in our runtime. They require confirmation by 2026-03-14.
Maya Chen (Security) 2026-03-11: +1 for scoped read-only run but require redaction plugin and pre-approved IAM role. Need proposed role ARN and list of engineers who will access.
Jonas Patel (SRE) 2026-03-11: I can create the inspector job. Suggest we use the existing job template 'kv-inspect-v3' which supports masking; will attach job plan as GH PR.
Aisha Kumar 2026-03-11: Adding audit requirement: record terminal session and upload to secure vault. CS will accept redaction proof rather than raw strings.

Maya Chen 2026-03-12: Security approves conditional access. Conditions: (a) max 6-hour window, (b) two named approvers must be present during run, (c) no downloads of raw outputs. Approver signatures required below.
notes_for_execution: Execution checklist: 1) Create IAM role with least privilege for admin-api:ReadKeys limited to resource ARNs for prefix. 2) Deploy kv-inspect-v3 with masking enabled; include regex for email, credit-card-like patterns, and 40+ char token hashes. 3) Start session in secure audit container; record and stream logs to audit S3 with server-side encryption. 4) Present redacted evidence to CS and update customer with findings; if value present, follow remediation SOP: rotate affected keys and communicate per privacy runbook.
